items.title: 1. Swallowed Too Much?: one clause of your poison control paragraph
items.question:
Your paragraph is in as you wrote it. One clause I'd say differently: "even if they often can't give actionable advice for liability reasons". What you told me is one case, about charcoal ("poison control said they aren't allowed to tell them to take charcoal"), and your next sentence says they do help with first aid instructions. [Poison Control's own page](https://www.poison.org/articles/2017-jun/activated-charcoal) says of charcoal that "it is not recommended to use these products at home to treat a poisoning", so anyone who asks them about it will hear what the person you know heard. This version says that, with the link on "they aren't allowed to tell anyone to take it", and reads [Human High, 74 words in one window](https://www.pangram.com/history/9afb6a77-e533-49d1-8f65-b20306e090ca) on its first check:
"If you're unsure about the interactions between the drugs taken, it could be helpful to check with AI & Poison Control. They might have important info, especially if the drugs are well-known. They can also help you with standard first aid instructions. But I wouldn't ask Poison Control about charcoal. Someone I know did, and came away very confused after being told they aren't allowed to tell anyone to take it."
(a) leave yours as it is; (b) this one; or your own words.

items.title: 2. My Acute Rescue Remedies: two things a reader in the moment couldn't tell
items.question:
This paragraph is in and reads [Human High, 75 words in one window](https://www.pangram.com/history/8f7d99cd-1a1e-4b29-b0e5-0b1e1659c02a); your post's read [AI, High](https://www.pangram.com/history/a378ba15-aee0-4b83-9ca8-702971cc31c6). Every sign is kept, and "a different branch" is now "the remedies below" and "the shadow work further down". Two things a fresh reader, sitting with a friend who has diarrhea and says their mind is going crazy, couldn't get from it, and only you know the answers:
2.1 What would a friend actually see when someone has "loss of bodily control" or "neurological disorganization"?
2.2 Diarrhea and nausea are common on a psychedelic anyway. How do you tell a gut-driven mental hell from a mainly emotional crisis while it is happening?
A line or two from you on either and I'll put it in; or (a) leave the paragraph as it is.
items.comment:
2.1 loss of bodily control includes urination, defecation, inability to sit up, stand, walk, talk, basically everything related to controlling the body. neurological disorganization is basically that plus a whole lot more it's a catch all term i will paste what gpt says the symptoms are:
**Neurological disorganization** is a broad, nonstandard clinical term describing difficulties coordinating, integrating or regulating nervous system activity. It is sometimes used in developmental neurology, neurorehabilitation and somatic therapies.

Symptoms can include:

### **Cognitive symptoms**

- Brain fog and mental confusion
- Difficulty organizing thoughts
- Impaired attention and working memory
- Slow information processing
- Difficulty making decisions
- Becoming overwhelmed by relatively simple tasks

### **Sensory symptoms**

- Hypersensitivity to light, sound, touch or smells
- Difficulty filtering background stimuli
- Altered body awareness (proprioception)
- Dizziness or spatial disorientation
- Difficulty integrating visual and auditory information

### **Motor symptoms**

- Poor balance and coordination
- Clumsiness
- Difficulty coordinating both sides of the body
- Muscle tension or abnormal muscle tone
- Tremors or involuntary movements
- Difficulty sequencing movements

### **Emotional and autonomic symptoms**

- Emotional instability
- Exaggerated startle response
- Difficulty transitioning between activation and relaxation
- Hypervigilance or shutdown
- Dissociation or depersonalization
- Irregular breathing patterns
- Disturbed sleep
- Abnormal sweating or heart-rate regulation
- Digestive disturbances

### **Potential underlying causes**

Neurological disorganization-like symptoms can occur with traumatic brain injury, developmental disorders, vestibular dysfunction, chronic traumatic stress, neuroinflammation, nutritional deficiencies, medication effects and various neurological diseases.

**Neurological disorganization versus nervous system dysregulation:** Dysregulation primarily concerns difficulty regulating physiological and emotional states, whereas disorganization is sometimes used more broadly to describe impaired coordination and integration across cognitive, sensory and motor systems. These are overlapping concepts, not formally distinct medical diagnoses.

Sudden onset of confusion, speech difficulties, weakness, severe imbalance or loss of coordination requires urgent medical assessment.

---
